title: On-Prem Support Escrow & Evidence Schedule (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This schedule is an attachment to the On-Premise Services Agreement. It defines the scope, procedures, and security controls for storing and delivering escrowed support materials and evidentiary artifacts that may be required to investigate incidents, demonstrate compliance, or support customer audits in on-prem deployments.

High-level intent / drafting notes (for reviewers):
- Keep the document focused on operational artifacts (logs, config exports, build manifests, signed binary hashes) rather than raw customer data.
- Where customer data is necessary for an investigation, include explicit access controls, minimization, and a separate DSAR/DFR process.
- Provide a clear transfer / handoff checklist so SRE + legal can execute under time pressure.
- This is an exhibit-level document; final language will be migrated into the DPA or Services Appendix as required.

Scope:
1) Covered artifacts: configuration snapshots, orchestration manifests, signed image digests, system-level logs (support window), audit traces (authentication/authorization streams), kernel dumps (only when required), secure debug packages, and signed build provenance documents.
2) Exclusions: end-user content, model weights, raw prompt/response datasets containing customer PII, and ephemeral telemetry retained solely for system health unless expressly requested under incident response.
3) Applicable environments: Customer-managed VPCs, air-gapped installations, and hybrid VPC-connected private deployments where Redwood personnel may need evidence access under the Support SLA.

Definitions (short):
- Escrowed Materials: Any artifact Redwood agrees to escrow or make available under this schedule.
- Evidence Package: Curated set of artifacts prepared for a specific incident, audit, or legal request.
- Support Window: Time-bounded period for which system logs are considered admissible under normal retention (default 30 days unless extended by contract).

Escrowed Materials & Retention Requirements:
- Configuration snapshots: point-in-time exported manifests (YAML/JSON) of orchestrator and runtime — retention default 365 days.
- Signed images and digests: immutable signed digests and provenance for builds used in customer environment — retention default 3 years.
- System-level logs and traces: rotated logs covering service-control plane and runtime errors — retention default 90 days; support packages may include a 365-day subset on request and subject to approval.
- Kernel / crash dumps: retained only for the incident lifecycle; persisted beyond the incident only with customer consent and legal sign-off.

Access & Delivery Procedures:
1) Request initiation: Support or customer submits a Support Evidence Request (SER) ticket (Jira/OPS or designated portal). Include: incident id, justification, expected artifacts, retention window.
2) Authorization: Requests require two approvers from Redwood: (a) SRE lead on-call and (b) Security compliance owner. If the request contains potential customer data, Legal must be looped in.
3) Packaging: SRE assembles a ZIP/TAR evidence package containing a manifest (Attachment A template), signed checksums, and a short analyst note describing retrieval steps. Packages are hashed and signed with Redwood code-signing key before transfer.
4) Transfer method: Prefer customer-supplied secure upload (S3 presigned URL with SSE-KMS or SFTP over mutual TLS). If Redwood initiates transfer, use ephemeral encrypted container and share a one-time key via a designated out-of-band channel.
5) Delivery SLA: Standard evidence requests: 5 business days. High-severity incidents (P1/P0): initial evidence payload within 24 hours and final package within 3 business days.

Security Controls for Escrow:
- Data minimization: Only include fields necessary for root cause analysis. Redact user content and PII where possible.
- Encryption: At-rest encryption using AES-256; transfer via TLS1.2+ with mutual auth. When storing in customer-provided S3, require SSE-KMS and deny permissive bucket ACLs.
- Key management: If Redwood holds keys for transfer, keys rotate per KMS schedule and access logs are retained. Key escrow to be handled by customer KMS where feasible.
- Isolation: Escrowed artifacts are stored in a dedicated, access-controlled bucket/project with logging and retention controls.

Evidence Access & Audit Rights:
- Customer access: Customers may request copies of evidence packages tied to incidents involving their environment. Access is subject to customer authentication and authorization checks.
- Audit / Third-party requests: Redwood will respond to lawful requests; for third-party audits, Redwood will seek customer consent unless legally compelled.
- Audit trail: All accesses to escrowed artifacts will be logged, with a retention window of at least 3 years for access metadata.

Breach Escalation & Notification:
- If artifacts include customer data and are accidentally exposed, Redwood will notify the customer within 48 hours of discovery (or sooner if required by law).
- Incident-specific communications plan will be used (see Incident Notification Timeline playbook).

Onsite Evidence Verification (for air-gapped/on-prem):
- If a customer requires onsite verification of artifacts, Redwood will coordinate a controlled onsite review with two Redwood representatives (one technical, one from security/compliance/legal if required).
- Onsite access is limited to inspection; copying artifacts off-prem requires explicit written consent and must follow transfer controls above.

Change Control & Versioning:
- Any change to the evidence inventory or retention defaults must be reflected in this schedule and require sign-off from Legal and Security.
- Escrow package formats and signing algorithms will be versioned; manifests must include format version and toolchain revision.

Liability and Remedies (summary for contract drafter):
- Redwood’s obligations are to make best efforts to preserve and deliver escrowed materials described here. Redwood is not liable for third-party tools installed by the customer that alter or delete artifacts prior to collection.
- Limitations of liability should reference the main SLA and DPA terms; consider a carve-out for cryptographic key compromise where customer-managed keys were used.

Operational attachments (drafts / templates):
- Attachment A: Evidence Package Manifest (fields: incident_id, collection_timestamp, artifacts_list, hashes, collector, approvers, packaging_version).
- Attachment B: Escrow Transfer Checklist (step-by-step ops checklist for packaging + transfer + verification).
- Attachment C: Redaction & Minimization Checklist (quick guide for SREs and support engineers).

Open questions / TODOs for next draft:
- Default retention windows: legal vs. sales negotiation floor. Suggest legal propose a minimum that balances auditability with risk (e.g., 90 days logs, 365 days config, 3 years image provenance).
- How to handle model artifacts that are derivative of customer data (need product input).
- Approval runway for onsite verification in highly regulated customers (lead time, NDAs, visitor control).
- Standardize evidence package signing key rotation cadence and emergency key revocation procedure.

References & links (working):
- Incident Notification Timeline and Communication Scripts (confluence.redwood/incident-notify)
- OnPrem Evidence Playbook (confluence.redwood/OnPrem-Evidence-Playbook-1234)
- JIRA: OPS-9876 (Support Evidence Requests)

Reviewer notes:
- Please comment inline on the "Deliver method" and "Retention" defaults — these are the two negotiation friction points we see with Sales and Legal in early enterprise deals.
- If product wants to treat model weights as "Provenance Only" (hashes + build manifests) rather than transferred artifacts, add explicit language in the exclusions section above.

Prepared by: Aisha Verma (security & compliance)
Draft status: internal draft for legal and SRE review

Attachment A - Evidence Package Manifest (template)
- incident_id: [string]
- collection_timestamp: [ISO 8601]
- environment: [customer-id or cluster-id]
- artifacts_list: [list of artifact filenames]
- artifact_hashes: [sha256 list]
- collector_name: [string]
- approver_names: [string list]
- signer: [redwood-code-signing-key-id]
- packaging_version: [v1.0]

Attachment B - Escrow Transfer Checklist (ops)
1) Verify SER authorization and approvals (SRE lead + security).
2) Pull manifests and minimal logs; run redaction checklist.
3) Generate checksums; sign package.
4) Upload to customer-provided secure location or prepare container for outbound transfer.
5) Confirm receipt with customer and attach receipt to SER ticket.
6) Log transfer in Escrow Access Log and mark package retention policy.

-- end draft --
